chunks: From him, from one of his companions, from Salih ibn Hamza, from Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah, from Abd Salih (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: 'Good neighbourliness is not merely refraining from causing harm, but good neighbourliness is your patience upon the harm (done to you by the neighbour).'

key_terms.حُسْنُ الْجِوَارِ: Good neighbourliness / Excellence in neighbourly relations
key_terms.صَبْرُكَ عَلَى الْأَذَى: Your patience upon the harm / Forbearance when harmed
key_terms.كَفَّ الْأَذَى: Refraining from causing harm / Restraint from annoyance

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between basic neighbourly conduct and true good neighbourliness in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration to distinguish between the baseline of 'kaff al-adha' (avoiding harm) and the superior ethic of 'sabr' (patience), reflecting the Shia emphasis on moral excellence (ihsan) in social relations. This hadith is frequently cited by scholars like Al-Majlisi to illustrate that true neighbourly rights are fulfilled not merely by neutrality, but by active forbearance during conflicts, aligning with the concept of 'sabr ala al-adha' found in broader Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
From him, from one of his companions, from Salih Bin Hamza, from Al Hassan Bin Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abd Salih<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:
‘Good neighbourliness is not restraint from harming (the neighbour), but good neighbourliness is your patience upon the harm (done to you by the neighbour)’.
en.sarwar: 8. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from al-Nahiki from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from al-Hakam al-Khayyat who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Maintaining good neighborly relations increases the development of the country and one’s life span.’”
